description: Auto-commit and push with apus, with every repository's status in plain sight.

walkthrough.title: Get started with Apus affinis
walkthrough.description: Let your repositories push themselves, and see how each one is doing.
walkthrough.connect.title: Connect apus
walkthrough.connect.description:
apus is the tool that does add + commit + push. Install it and tell the extension where it is — if it is on your PATH, it is found on its own.
[Download apus](command:apus.downloadApus)
[Choose apus binary…](command:apus.selectBinary)
walkthrough.connect.alt: The apus icon connected to a VS Code window.
walkthrough.watch.title: Add a repository and watch it
walkthrough.watch.description:
Add the folder of a project with + in the Apus view: each repository shows its folder, the URL it pushes to and its branch, and a click on the folder or the URL changes it. Watching is off by default: pushing on its own is your call, one repository at a time.
[Add Folder…](command:apus.addFolder)
[Watch a Repository](command:apus.toggleWatch)
walkthrough.watch.alt: The Apus view: one repository open as a card with its folder, URL and branch, and another one held back by a .env file.
walkthrough.safety.title: Nothing sensitive goes up
walkthrough.safety.description:
Before every push, apus looks at what is about to leave your machine: .env files, private keys, tokens pasted into a file and files too big for GitHub. An auto-commit pushes nothing while one is there, and a push by hand asks first. Each finding comes with its fix: add it to .gitignore, stop tracking it, or let a false positive through.
[Review Held Files](command:apus.reviewHeld)
walkthrough.safety.alt: A shield in front of git push, and the list of held files: a .env, a token in config.ts and a 180 MB file.
walkthrough.status.title: Read the status bar
walkthrough.status.description:
From top to bottom: up to date, with the time of the last push · changes waiting and the countdown to the next auto-commit · paused · pushing · held back, because something should not be pushed · something needs your attention. Hover for details and quick actions, click for the menu.
[Open the menu](command:apus.menu)
walkthrough.status.alt: Six status bar items showing the states of apus.
walkthrough.rules.title: Tune the rules
walkthrough.rules.description:
How long to wait after your last change, the minimum time between auto-commits, which files do not count, the commit message and which notifications to show.
[Open rules](command:apus.openSettings)
walkthrough.rules.alt: The apus settings: intervals, ignored patterns and notifications.
commands.explainNested: Why a Repository Inside Is a Problem
config.autoStart: Watch repositories as soon as they open. When off, each repository is watched by hand from the menu or the **Apus** view.
config.watchInterval: Seconds without new changes before auto-committing.
config.minInterval: Minimum seconds between two auto-commits of the same repository, even across windows.
config.ignorePatterns: Globs, relative to the repository root, whose changes **do not trigger** an auto-commit (for example `*.log` or `docs/**`). If there are other changes, everything is pushed together: to keep files out of git, use `.gitignore`.
config.messageTemplate: Auto-commit message. `{date}` becomes the date and time. The trailer `Apus-Auto: true` is appended so auto-commits can be recognized later.
config.checkBeforePush: Before every push, look at what is about to go up: `.env` files, private keys, tokens pasted into a file (GitHub, AWS, OpenAI, Anthropic and others) and files too big for GitHub. An auto-commit pushes nothing while one is there, and a push by hand asks first. Only your user settings can change this: a repository cannot turn it off.
config.maxFileSize: Largest file, in MB, that can be pushed. GitHub rejects files over 100 MB and warns from 50 MB.
config.notifications.off: Never: the status stays in the status bar and the view.
config.path: Path to the apus binary (`apus.exe` on Windows). Empty: search the `PATH`.
